title: Microfluidic Fabrication of Core-Shell Microcapsules carrying Human Pluripotent Stem Cell Spheroids
protocol: Make the designs for the microencapsulation device and dissociation device using CAD software.
Spin-coat a clean 10 cm silicon wafer with SU-8 2025 negative photoresist at 1,100 rpm to create the first 60 µm layer.
Soft bake the mold at 65 °C for 3 min and then at 95 °C for 10 min on a hot plate.
Expose the mold using a maskless aligner by uploading the design file of the core channel pattern.
Post-exposure bake the mold at 65 °C for 3 min and then at 95 °C for 10 min.
Spin coat the second SU-8 2025 layer (40 µm) at 1,500 rpm and expose by uploading the appropriate CAD file for the shell channel pattern.
Soft bake and post-exposure bake the mold as in previous steps.
Spin coat the third SU-8 2025 layer at 1,400 rpm to achieve 50 µm height.
Expose the structures for the oil phase using a maskless aligner by uploading the appropriate CAD file.
Develop the mold with all three layers in a single step by submersion in SU-8 developer until unexposed photoresist is removed.
Hard bake the mold on a hot plate at 160 °C for 10 min to improve adhesion and seal minor cracks.
Expose the mold to chlorotrimethylsilane.
Place the mold in 15 cm Petri dishes until use.
Spin coat one layer of SU-8 photoresist on a silicon wafer.
Conduct the soft and post-exposure bake, development, and hard bake similarly to previous steps.
Mix PDMS elastomer base and elastomer curing agent in a 10:1 w/w ratio.
Pour the mixture onto both microencapsulation master molds and dissociation master mold to create a 3-4 mm layer.
Place the Petri dishes containing the molds in a vacuum desiccator for 15 min.
Move the Petri dishes to an oven and bake at 80 °C for a minimum of 60 min.
Remove master molds from the oven and allow them to cool down.
Cut PDMS following the shape of the wafer using a precision knife.
Peel out PDMS pieces from the master mold.
Trim edges of each device with a scalpel.
Punch inlet fluidic ports in the dissociation device using a 14 G needle.
Punch outlet fluidic ports in the top microfluidic device using a 15 G needle.
Cover devices with magic tape to avoid contamination.
Treat patterned sides of the top and bottom PDMS pieces with O2 plasma for 2 min.
Add a thin separating layer of distilled water (2 µL) directly in the microchannels.
Align both PDMS parts under a stereoscope.
Place aligned PDMS device in the oven at 80 °C overnight.
Inject 30 µL of hydrophobic coating solution into fluidic channels immediately after bonding.
Purge air into the channels until no residues of the hydrophobic coating solution are observed.
Bond the dissociation device by treating the patterned side with O2 plasma for 2 min.
Bond the cleaned slide glass to the treated side of the device.
Assemble the bonded device and cure it in an oven at 80 °C overnight.
Prepare 30 mL of 2x core solution: mix 4.8 g of 35 kDa PEG, 10.2 mL of density gradient media, and 19.8 mL of DMEM/F12 media.
Filter the prepared core solution using a 0.22 μm syringe filter.
Prepare 50 mL of mineral oil with 3% surfactant: mix 48.5 mL of mineral oil and 1.5 mL of surfactant.
Filter this mixture through a 0.22 µm syringe filter to maintain sterility.
Prepare 50 mL of mineral oil with 0.5% surfactant: mix 49.75 mL of mineral oil and 0.25 mL of surfactant.
Filter the prepared solution through a 0.22 μm syringe filter to ensure sterility.
Prepare 1 M Dithiotheritol (DTT): dissolve 1.5425 g of DTT in 10 mL distilled water.
Keep the DTT solution sterile after preparation.
Prepare 1 M Triethanolamine (TEA): add 66.4 µL of TEA to 433.6 µL of distilled water.
Maintain sterility by preparing and handling carefully.
Prepare 1% Pluronic F127 (PF127): dissolve 100 mg of PF127 in 10 mL of distilled water.
Ensure the solution is sterile after preparation.
Mix 4.5 mL of mineral oil with 3% surfactant and 300 µL of 1 M DTT in a 1:15 ratio.
Vortex the solution for 2 minutes.
Sonicate the solution for 45-60 minutes in an ultrasonic bath at 20 °C.
Load the emulsion to a 5 mL syringe with a 27 G needle.
Prepare shielding oil solution by loading mineral oil with 0.5% surfactant into a 5 mL syringe with a 27 G needle.
Add 32 mg of PEG-4-Mal to 400 µL of 1x DPBS to form an 8% w/v solution.
Vortex the PEG-4-Mal and DPBS mixture for 2 minutes.
Add 6 µL of 1 M TEA (final concentration 15 mM TEA) to the PEG-4-Mal solution.
Centrifuge the solution at 13,000 x g for 5 minutes through a spin-filter.
Keep the PEG-4-Mal and TEA solution in the dark on the rocker for 30 minutes.
Load the shell solution into a 1 mL syringe with a 27 G needle.
Leave the PEG-4-Mal container at room temperature for 10 minutes before opening the lid.
Blow N2 gas to replace O2 with N2 before closing the lid of the PEG-4-Mal container.
Vortex TEA before adding it to the shell solution.
Treat hPSCs with trypsin for 5 to 10 minutes at 37 °C.
Collect cells from plates after treatment.
Quench the trypsin with medium after cell detachment.
Transfer the cells to a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the bulk cell suspension at 400 x g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant carefully.
Resuspend the cell pellet using a minimal volume of growth medium.
Count the cells using an automated cell counter.
Take 12-20 x 10^6 cells from the bulk cell suspension.
Centrifuge the cell/media suspension at 400 x g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate media from the cell pellet.
Add 200 µL of medium and 200 µL of a 2x PEG solution (final concentration: 30-50 x 10^6 cells/mL).
Mix gently.
Add 30 µL of 1% PF127 to the solution.
Insert a micro stirrer bar into a 1 mL syringe.
Load the cell-containing core solution into the syringe with a 27 G needle.
Keep the solution cold with ice during the encapsulation process.
Place bonded PDMS droplet device beneath a germicidal light source.
Sterilize for 30 minutes using forceps to fit tubing into fluidic inlet ports and dissociation ports.
Use 20 cm long microtubes for shell, oil, and crosslinker emulsion inlets.
Insert one end of the tubes into the needle of the syringe with corresponding solution.
Connect a 5 cm microtube between the core inlet of the device and the outlet of the dissociation device.
Securely insert each end of the inlet microtubes within fitting tubes attached to syringes.
Place an outlet tube into the fluidic outlet port and position the other end in a collection reservoir.
Mount the microfluidic device on a microscope stage.
Attach tubing securely to avoid movement during operation.
Align and focus the microscope on the device nozzle for flow inspection.
Position each syringe on different syringe pumps and secure them properly.
Program each pump according to manufacturer's protocols with core (3-5 µL/min), shell (3-5 µL/min), shielding oil (20-80 µL/min), and crosslinking oil (40-60 µL/min) flow rates.
Start the flow in all pumps simultaneously.
Wait for fluids to enter the device and fill up channels while expelling remaining air.
Place the opposite end of the collection tube into a new conical tube containing 5 mL mTeSR media.
Incubate capsules in a new conical tube at 37 °C with 5% CO2 for 10 min.
Gently tap on the tube to cause capsules to sediment to the bottom.
Aspirate most of the oil and media from the top of the tubes containing settled capsules.
Collect the capsules from the bottom of the conical tube, place them on a cell strainer (100 μm pore size).
Wash the collected capsules with copious amounts of media.
Invert the cell strainer on top of a 6-well culture plate filled with 2 mL mTeSR media to collect microcapsules.
Incubate stem cell capsules in a 6-well plate culture dish at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Change the media every other day by collecting capsules, washing them thoroughly, and resuspending them in fresh media.
Culture the capsules for at least 10 days.
Thaw live/dead assay solutions (ethidium homodimer-1 and calcein AM).
Add 4 μL of the 2 μM ethidium homodimer-1 solution to 2 mL of sterile DPBS.
Add 1 μL of the 4 μM calcein AM solution to the mixture.
Vortex the solution to ensure complete mixing.
Collect approximately 100 microcapsules on a cell strainer.
Rinse the collected microcapsules with sterile DPBS.
Transfer the rinsed microcapsules using 1 mL of the prepared solution to a 12 well culture plate.
Incubate at 37 °C for 20 min.
Visualize the cells under a fluorescence microscope.
